description.text: A New Type of Biopharmaceutical Company BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. is a commercial-stage, multi-product biopharmaceutical company organized around a portfolio operating model to discover, develop, and deliver medicines for patients with genetic diseases. We seek to translate advances in genetic science into therapies for patient populations with significant unmet medical needs. Since our founding 10 years ago, we have advanced multiple programs from discovery through regulatory approval and commercialization. To date, more than 8,500 patients have been treated with our approved medicines, and we have obtained U.S. Food and Drug Administration (the “FDA”) approval for three products. We believe our decentralized hub and spoke model enables us to achieve clinical proof-of-concept with speed and efficiency, demonstrated by an average investment per program of less than $40.0 million to proof-of-concept data and less than $10.0 million to reach Investigational New Drug (“IND”) submission. This efficiency allows us to work on a broad range of scientifically compelling therapies, including programs for underserved conditions which more traditional biopharmaceutical models might leave on the shelf but we believe can be developed on a Net Present Value (“NPV”)-positive basis in our portfolio.

about.description_short: BridgeBio exists to develop transformative medicines for genetic conditions. Millions of people worldwide living with genetic conditions lack treatment options, often because drug development for small patient populations can be commercially challenging. We aim to bridge the gap between advancements in genetic science and meaningful medicines for underserved patient populations. Our decentralized, hub-and-spoke model is designed for speed, precision, and scalability. Autonomous and empowered teams focus on individual conditions, while a central hub provides the clinical, regulatory, and commercial capabilities needed to bring innovation to market.

analysis_md:
# BBIO — BridgeBio Pharma, Inc.
v5 run (engine 5.4.0), 2026-10-17. In scope (market cap $12,715,509,530 at $66.39, nasdaq_quote_api — engine figure).

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, ttm.py output, fundamentals.json, or the cited company releases — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company (Palo Alto) built on a hub-and-spoke model for genetic diseases. Its one marketed product is Attruby (acoramidis), an oral near-complete (≥90%) transthyretin stabilizer approved in Nov 2024 for transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), sold ex-U.S. by partners as Beyonttra with royalties back to BridgeBio. It competes with Pfizer's Vyndaqel/Vyndamax and Alnylam's Amvuttra. Three more Phase-3-positive programs are in FDA review: BBP-418 for LGMD2I/R9 (PDUFA Nov 27, 2026), encaleret for ADH1 (PDUFA May 8, 2027), and oral infigratinib for achondroplasia (NDA submitted, U.S. launch expected mid-2027) — all per the Q2 2026 results release (SEC Ex-99.1).

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow −$445,910,000; capex $1,097,000 (asset-light — the burn is R&D/SG&A, not plant); SBC $133,024,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: −$580,031,000 = −$3.03/share** (base_oe_latest_per_share −3.0284478965791446).
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): −$783,069,000 — even worse, because FY2025 net income carries large noncash financing charges (see NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE). The two definitions disagree on size, not sign.
- **OE positive in 0 of the last 5 fiscal years.** Normalized base (median of last 3 FY OE/share) = **−$3.32/share** (base_oe_normalized_per_share −3.3183184366949066) — the base used, because it is the engine standard and every alternative base is also negative (see STALE_FY). No scenario DCF is supportable: the engine emits no IV or IRR for any scenario when the normalized base is negative, and the tier is F by definition (no positive conservative owner's earnings; F sub-type: no_cash_generation — OCF − capex is not positive over the median window).
- The trajectory is genuinely improving, which is the bull case in one line: Q2 2026 total revenue $243.7M (+120.4% YoY), of which U.S. Attruby net product revenue $222.4M (+211.1% YoY) at a 95.3% product gross margin, and the quarterly operating loss narrowed to −$107.1M (Q2 2026 results release). Revenue growth has not yet outrun a cost base built to launch four products at once: FY2025 R&D was $451,953,000 and SG&A $531,225,000 against revenue of $502,076,000 (FY2025 results release / 10-K).
- Balance sheet (engine, FY2025 end): total debt $2,007,337,000 (basis TOTAL:LongTermDebt) against cash $570,119,000 → **net debt $1,437,218,000**; lease liabilities $10,003,000; stockholders' equity **−$2,086,610,000**. Cash, equivalents and marketable securities were $587,482,000 at Dec 31, 2025 (10-K). The claim stack has grown since: $632.5M of 2033 convertible notes issued in January 2026, and $933.9M of 7% Series A preferred stock raised July 1, 2026 (conversion price $137.79) — both senior to the common being valued, neither in the FY2025 engine figures. Cash and securities stood at $720.2M at June 30, 2026 before the preferred raise (Q2 2026 release).

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow, a real product franchise not yet proven in cash
Justification: Attruby is a differentiated, patent-protected product taking first-line share in a growing category at ~95% product gross margins, and the same development engine has produced three more Phase-3-positive assets — but the franchise is one product, the two competitors are far larger, and there is no year of positive operating income in the company's history to prove the economics survive competition.
- FOR: Near-complete (≥90%) TTR stabilization — the differentiation claim versus tafamidis — with first-line share still climbing and real-world data associating acoramidis with fewer cardiovascular events/hospitalizations than tafamidis (Q2 2026 release); product gross margin 95.3% in Q2 2026 and total gross margin 95.82% FY2025 / 98.25% FY2024 (fundamentals.json) — pricing power is real at the product level; ex-U.S. royalty stream (Beyonttra) with zero commercial cost; a repeatable rare-disease development platform — three additional NDAs in FDA review at once (BBP-418, encaleret, infigratinib).
- AGAINST: Single-product concentration — Attruby is essentially all product revenue; Pfizer (Vyndaqel/Vyndamax, the entrenched incumbent) and Alnylam (Amvuttra) are larger, better-capitalized competitors in the same category; **no ROIC evidence**: operating income has been negative every fiscal year on file (FY2025 −$523,411,000), equity is −$2,086,610,000, and the roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json prints positive values only because its equity + debt − cash denominator is distorted by the negative equity — it is an artifact, not a return on capital; heavy and growing claim stack ahead of common (convertibles, deferred royalty obligations, 7% preferred) plus 9.1%/yr share dilution.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years — moot here, since there is no positive base OE to project.

## DCF — v5 final run (2026-10-17)
Final engine pass run with --moat 5 --probs 0.10/0.25/0.30/0.25/0.10 (defaults retained; offsets/multipliers not applicable). Price $66.39.
- **No scenario table exists for this name, by design:** with normalized base OE of −$3.32/share, latest-FY −$3.03/share, and TTM −$2.98/share, the engine produces no IV@15% and no implied IRR in any scenario — super bear through super bull all scale a negative base. Growth optics are equally unusable: revenue CAGR 5y 127.47% / 3y 86.27% and latest YoY +126.26% are measured off the pre-Attruby base (FY2023 revenue was $9,303,000) and are launch artifacts, not a growth rate.
- **Tier by numbers: F** (F sub-type: no_cash_generation). Probability-weighted IV/IRR: not emitted (null in dcf_numbers.json).
- Diagnostics: OE positive 0/5 years; share count CAGR 9.1%/yr; net debt $1,437,218,000 at FY end.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 2025-12-31, ~10 months ago): resolved with ttm.py, whose full output is saved in ttm.json. TTM inputs (FY − prior YTD + current YTD, current YTD ended 2026-06-30): OCF FY −$445,910,000, prior YTD −$279,916,000, current YTD −$268,380,000 → TTM −$434,374,000. Capex FY $1,097,000, prior YTD $594,000, current YTD $512,000 → TTM $1,015,000. SBC FY $133,024,000, prior YTD $63,123,000, current YTD $77,314,000 → TTM $147,215,000. Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted) 195,290,642. **TTM OE total −$582,604,000 → −$2.98/share** — the least negative of the three bases (operating leverage is starting to show), but still negative, so the F verdict does not depend on base choice and no --ttm pin was applied.
- **DILUTION** (share count +9.1%/yr): real and continuing. Diluted shares per the filed history: 162,791,511 (FY2023) → 186,075,873 (FY2024) → 191,527,482 (FY2025) → 195,290,642 (H1 2026 YTD, ttm.py); shares outstanding (dei) 195,487,474 as of 2026-08-03. SBC is rising with it — $133,024,000 FY2025 → $147,215,000 TTM — and the July 2026 preferred is convertible at $137.79. The engine's −5pp growth adjustment for the share trend is moot on a negative base; the point for the verdict is that any future positive OE gets divided by a count still growing ~9%/yr.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT** (>60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs): not a divestiture, M&A, or restatement — it is a product launch. Revenue was license/services-only and lumpy before Attruby ($40,560,000 FY2019 → $8,249,000 FY2020 → $9,303,000 FY2023), then product revenue began with the Nov 2024 approval: $221,902,000 FY2024 → $502,076,000 FY2025 → $243.7M in Q2 2026 alone. All revenue CAGRs in dcf_numbers.json straddle the launch and were not used for any growth input.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2025): explained by noncash financing and comp charges inside net income that are added back in OCF, per the FY2025 results release / 10-K reconciliation: noncash interest expense on deferred royalty obligations $125,138,000 (vs $8,299,000 in FY2024 — the royalty financing was struck in 2025), SBC $133,024,000, net loss from equity-method investments $72,608,000, and loss on extinguishments of debt $21,155,000. That is why net income (−$732,938,000) runs far below OCF (−$445,910,000) without either being wrong. The conservative OE base is built from OCF and deducts SBC separately, so the divergence does not flatter or contaminate the base — and note the royalty-obligation accretion is a real economic claim on future Attruby cash flows even though it is noncash today.
- **SHARES_FALLBACK** (no diluted count filed for 2018, 2019): those two history years use the outstanding count recorded in the shares_tag column of financials_history.csv; per-share history there is approximate. All recent years (FY2023 onward) use filed diluted counts, so the bases above are unaffected.

## My thoughts / overlay
- This is the rare F where the business is visibly working: Attruby is annualizing above $1B of revenue at ~95% product gross margin within two years of launch, and three more approvals could land between Nov 2026 and mid-2027. The OE-DCF still has nothing to grip — five straight years of negative owner's earnings on both definitions, a TTM base of −$2.98/share, and H1 2026 operating cash use of $268,380,000 (ttm.json current-YTD leg).
- The gap between the product economics and the shareholder economics is the story: a ~95%-gross-margin drug is being carried by a cost base sized for four simultaneous launches and a claim stack (convertibles, royalty obligations, 7% preferred) that keeps layering ahead of the common. Management's own framing (Q4 2025 call reporting) has the pipeline turning cash-generative in late 2027 — until a filed quarter shows positive OCF, that is a forecast, not a base.
- There is no hurdle-clearing price to quote: with negative owner's earnings at every base, no positive price produces a 15% OE-implied return. The 15% question only becomes askable after the company prints its first positive-OE year; until then any entry price is paying for launch execution and pipeline optionality, not cash flows.
- Sizing: the F is a statement about the screen, not a short thesis — commercial-stage biotechs mid-launch fail this screen by construction. But on Andrew's hurdles there is nothing here to underwrite today, and the next hard evidence is binary and dated: BBP-418 PDUFA Nov 27, 2026.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: F** (no positive normalized owner's earnings — 0/5 years, every base negative: median −$3.32, latest FY −$3.03, TTM −$2.98 per share)
- Confidence: **Medium** (the F arithmetic is unambiguous on filed data; anything forward-looking about this name is binary on approvals and launch execution, so the overall call is not high-confidence)
- One-liner: Commercial-stage rare-disease biotech with a real, fast-growing Attruby franchise and moat 5/10, but owner's earnings are negative on every base (TTM −$2.98/sh, 0/5 positive years) and debt, royalty and preferred claims keep stacking ahead of the common — no positive price clears the 15% hurdle until it prints a positive-OE year.
